title: Sell Mineral Rights in Andrews, TX
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Andrews, TX | Royalty Buyer
metaDescription: Andrews, TX sits over decades of layered oil production. A retired engineer explains what actually drives a fair offer on your mineral or royalty interest.
heroLead: Andrews is a real working town, the county seat, with an oilfield service economy that's been steady for generations rather than boom-and-bust.
intro: Unlike some of the smaller crossroads communities scattered through this county, Andrews has enough population and infrastructure to function as the actual hub of Andrews County's oilfield activity. If your family has owned minerals here for a while, there's a decent chance the checks have been coming in some form since before horizontal drilling even existed, layered now under newer Wolfcamp production.

sections.heading: Layered production near town
paragraphs: A lot of the acreage in and around Andrews carries production history going back to older vertical Spraberry and San Andres wells, some of which are still pumping today at modest rates, now sitting alongside newer horizontal Wolfcamp units drilled on the same or adjacent sections. If your check reflects both, I look at each contributing well separately rather than treating the blended number as one simple decline curve.

sections.heading: What moves your number
paragraphs: Net royalty acres, current production, and how close your specific tract sits to recent horizontal development around Andrews are the main drivers. A recent check stub or division order lets me pull the real well history instead of estimating, so that's the fastest way to get an honest range from me.

sections.heading: If you inherited this from family in town
paragraphs: It's common in Andrews for a mineral interest to be split among several heirs who grew up in town but have since scattered. I can typically buy your individual share without requiring the rest of the family to participate, and I'll walk you through what documentation clears title on an inherited interest.

faqs.question: My check seems to come from an old well, is that interest still worth anything?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, especially if there's newer horizontal development nearby. Legacy vertical production still generates real, if modest, royalty income and I value it against actual data rather than dismissing it.

faqs.question: How do I know if I own royalty or a working interest?
faqs.answer: Check your division order or the statement itself. Royalty interests don't carry cost deductions for drilling or operating expenses; working interests do. Send it to me and I'll tell you plainly which you hold.

faqs.question: Can you buy just my share if my siblings don't want to sell?
faqs.answer: Yes. I regularly purchase one heir's fractional interest without the rest of the family needing to be involved.
